sentence: This project supports developmental biology research and expands imaging and bioinformatics services for researchers studying the molecular basis of many diseases.
This project tries to find specific RNA molecules that could treat human disease, using gene transfer and oligonucleotide delivery in model systems.
This project uses machine learning on clinical and biological data to find lung transplant patients at high risk of graft dysfunction earlier.
This project builds a tool that adjusts the phase of each transmit channel to improve phosphorus magnetic spectroscopy imaging of the human brain.
This project studies the role of three molecular mechanisms in persistent atrial fibrillation, a heart rhythm disorder, and uses genes to target them.
This project builds a gene therapy for cystic fibrosis using adeno-associated viral vectors.
This project builds tools to test how to prevent fretting-corrosion in the modular junctions of total joint replacements.
This project studies how the immune system interacts with oral cancer and how tumors change the immune response.
This project supports a cancer center that does research, prevention and treatment work, including clinical trials, to reduce cancer incidence and mortality.
This project provides imaging services for the living eyes of rodent models, helping researchers study eye function and disease.
This project tries to find out what controls self-renewing T cells that respond to checkpoint blockade therapy in patients with malignant melanoma.
This project studies how mitochondria released from cells are cleared, focusing on a complement component made by neutrophils.
This project studies how tuft cells in the intestine are regulated, to guide therapeutic approaches for inflammatory bowel diseases.
This project tries to improve spin-based quantum sensors so they can study oxidative stress and iron regulation inside single cells.
This project studies a part of the stimulatory G protein as a treatment target in myelodysplastic syndromes with splicing factor mutations.
This project breeds mice with mutations caused by N-ethyl-N nitrosourea and watches them for disease, then freezes sperm from them.
This project builds mouse models to study and overcome the immune barriers to transplantation using genetics.
This project studies how receptor tyrosine kinases and their trafficking inside cells control chaperone-mediated autophagy, which breaks down proteins in lysosomes.
This project studies how CRISPR systems in bacteria pick their targets when defending against viruses and how this affects genome editing.
This project maps gene expression across the immune system and studies how its regulation relates to immune responses.
